items.title: How many warning-sign categories does it take before a pattern is worth acting on?
items.description: Priya's case involved all three categories at once — shifting goalposts, exclusion from key threads, and sudden isolation — over six weeks. Drag the slider to see how confidence that something real is going on changes as more independent categories show up simultaneously, holding duration and the alternative-explanation check fixed at 'no innocent explanation survives.' One category alone stays low-confidence noise territory; three together is where L2's framework says a real pattern is worth taking seriously.

outputs.label: Confidence this is a real, deliberate pattern

items.title: How much should a signal's duration count toward calling it a real pattern?
items.description: In Priya's timeline, the scope change and the meeting exclusion together spanned six weeks before she wrote the pattern down. This demo reproduces that scale: as a suspected signal persists for more weeks, drag the slider to see how much weight it should carry in your overall read — a single bad week (around week 1) barely moves the needle, but a signal still showing up six or more weeks later, per L2's duration check, is doing real work in the multiplicity-plus-duration-plus-alternative-explanation case for a real pattern.
items.compute: const weight = Math.min(100, Math.round(100 * (1 - Math.exp(-params.weeksPersisted / 3)))); return { weight };
